methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective cohort study with n=210 (190 with complete follow-up), double-blind sample collection, and appropriate risk stratification frameworks. Methods well-described with proper ethics approval and informed consent. Limitations acknowledged: single-center design and modest sample sizes for subgroups (n=8 metastatic patients). Statistical methods appropriate with ROC analysis, log-rank testing, and Spearman correlation, though explicit power calculation statement absent.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual prospective cohort study directly addressing clinical challenge of preoperative PTC risk stratification. Dual-threshold CTC model provides actionable clinical decision-making: cutoff ≥1 CTC for rule-out (NPV=92.5%), ≥2 CTCs for rule-in (PPV=80%, specificity=96.4%) in PTMC. Enables personalized therapy selection between active surveillance and aggressive surgery. Long median follow-up (44 months) demonstrates clinical relevance.

reporting_quality.justification: Clear adherence to STROBE reporting standard with detailed patient cohort description, inclusion/exclusion criteria, ethics approval, outcome definitions, and statistical methods explicitly stated. Figure legends and supplementary data referenced throughout. No explicit data availability statement or code sharing mentioned; methods section sufficient for replication but raw data not committed to repository.

novelty_literature.justification: First application of CTC detection for preoperative (not postoperative) PTC risk stratification, extending prior literature on CTCs for prognosis and recurrence monitoring. Dual-threshold model is novel adaptation, and PTMC-specific analysis addresses clinical gap. However, CTC technology platform itself and basic biology already established; contribution is primarily in clinical application and stratification framework.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear abstract, logical progression through introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Figures 1-6 effectively communicate technical validation, clinical correlations, and survival outcomes. Supplementary figures appropriately referenced. Minor opportunity: key clinical findings on PTMC could be elevated in main results. Overall publication-ready with appropriate level of detail and clarity.

key_strengths: Prospective design with double-blind CTC detection and long median follow-up (44 months) demonstrating prognostic signal
Dual-threshold decision model (≥1 for rule-out, ≥2 for rule-in) directly translatable to clinical practice with clear NPV/PPV profiles
Special focus on PTMC subgroup (n=100) addresses real clinical controversy over active surveillance vs. definitive therapy with novel biological data
Robust technical validation of TUMORFISHER platform across cell lines and clinical specimens with sensitivity/specificity analysis
key_concerns: Single-center study from China; results platform-specific (TUMORFISHER); requires multicenter external validation before widespread implementation
Small cohort of metastatic patients (n=8) limits generalizability of findings for distant metastasis prediction; authors acknowledge this limitation
Retrospective elements present despite prospective design characterization; no explicit pre-registration or protocol statement
No data availability statement; inability to assess raw data or reproduce exact calculations
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 paper demonstrates competent methodology with direct clinical relevance and meaningful incremental contribution to PTC management, but requires multicenter validation and larger metastatic subgroup before higher-tier consideration. Solid for regional/specialty journals in oncology.
